[docs/events.md#schedule]
The handler gets `event.type == "schedule"` and `event.data == input`. pskit converts the portable syntax to each cloud's dialect: A rate that can't be expressed as cron on cron-only clouds (e.g. `7 minutes`) fails validation; use a divisor of 60 minutes or 24 hours. `timezone` is honoured by AWS, GCP and Alibaba (cron form); Azure ignores it with a warning.

[docs/configuration.md#variables]
- `${tf:<terraform expression>}` becomes a live Terraform reference, e.g. `${tf:aws_dynamodb_table.orders.arn}` in an IAM statement or environment value. Every other `${` in user values is escaped, so Terraform never interprets it. - Any other `${...}`, such as IAM policy variables like `${aws:username}`, stays literal.

[docs/studio.md#saving-what-changes-in-pskityml]
- Values keep their written form: `${env:API_KEY}`, `${self:custom.x}` and `${opt:...}` are saved as written, never resolved. - Comments are **not** kept, and key order follows the studio's layout. Before every save the previous file is copied to `.pskit/studio/backups/pskit.<timestamp>.yml` (the last 20 are kept). - If `pskit.yml` changed on disk since you loaded it (an editor, `git pull`), Save offers to reload, overwrite or cancel. - A file that uses `extends:` is shown with a notice: only the main file is edited. - A config that fails validation can still be saved, so you can stop half-way. The problems stay listed.

[docs/smtp/README.md#create-it]
In the studio: **Resources → + SMTP server**. Already receive mail on your root domain (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace)? Use a **subdomain** such as `inbound.example.com`. Changing the root domain's MX would stop every mailbox of the company from receiving mail. From the command line it is the same service: It adds this to `pskit.yml`: Deploy (`pskit deploy`) so the host knows the trigger.

[docs/studio.md#full-vs-code-code-server-in-docker]
1. Studio checks for the Docker CLI and a running daemon. If either is missing, it shows how to install Docker. 2. **Pull & start** pulls the image if it isn't present (the log streams in the panel), then starts `pskit-studio-<id>` with your project mounted at `/home/coder/project`, published on `127.0.0.1` only, and waits until it answers. 3. The editor opens inside the studio, with **Open in new tab** and **Stop**. A container that's already running is reused. Stop removes it; your files stay in the project folder.
